concept: Ruby driver CRUD and connection management

claims.text: Coinbase reported in June 2020 that its Ruby processes each maintained a MongoDB pool shared by that process’s threads, and that blue-green deployment overlap increased the database connection count. This is a historical production example of connection multiplication across processes and deployment replicas. (low confidence)
Construct a Mongo::Client with a MongoDB connection URI; most applications can reuse a single client across multiple requests because it owns connection pools. (medium confidence)
Call client.close when finished, or construct the client with a Ruby block so it closes automatically when the block finishes. (low confidence)

Coinbase reported in its June 18, 2020 case study that per-process Ruby pools and overlapping blue-green deployments multiplied MongoDB connections. It introduced a connection proxy after finding many connections mostly unused; this is historical workload evidence, not a general requirement to deploy a proxy. (low confidence)
Use insert_one for a single document and insert_many for a list of documents. (low confidence)
Use delete_one to remove the first matching document and delete_many to remove all matching documents; both accept a query filter. (medium confidence)

Use insert_one for a single document and insert_many for a list of documents. If the application does not supply _id, the driver can generate unique BSON::ObjectId values; duplicate _id values violate the unique index. (low confidence)

Use update_one for the first matching document and update_many for all matches, supplying a query filter and an update document such as a $set operation. Set upsert: true to insert when no document matches. (low confidence)

Ordered bulk writes stop after a write-operation failure. With ordered: false, the driver attempts all specified operations and reports write errors after those attempts; execution order is not guaranteed. (medium confidence)
Iterate query results with each to consume a cursor that holds a subset of results in memory; chained limit and sort options refine the query results. (low confidence)

Update results distinguish matched_count from modified_count: an identical document is excluded from modified_count. Check acknowledged? before reading other result methods; an unacknowledged result cannot provide those values. (low confidence)

Collection#bulk_write accepts a list of operation hashes, including insert_one, update_one, update_many, replace_one, delete_one and delete_many. Ordered execution stops after a write error; ordered: false attempts the remaining operations without guaranteeing execution order. (low confidence)

A pool limit is not a deployment-wide connection limit: the Ruby pool guide also describes monitoring connections outside the application pool, and Coinbase documented separate pools for Ruby processes, shared by their threads. (medium confidence)

The server-selection guide describes filtering read candidates by read preference, applying the localThresholdMS latency window, and selecting randomly among remaining candidates. For writes it starts with writable servers rather than read-preference matches. (low confidence)

The pool guide conflicts with the connection-options reference and client source on max_idle_time units: its detailed example calls 10000 milliseconds ten seconds, whereas the reference maps max_idle_time: 10 to maxIdleTimeMS=10000 and the client source documents seconds. Treat the pool-guide example as conflicting documentation rather than a safe Ruby configuration to copy. (low confidence)

Collection#find accepts a query filter and returns a Mongo::Collection::View; execution is deferred until results are requested with first or each. Chain first to retrieve one matching document. (low confidence)
update_one changes the first matching document; update_many changes all matching documents. Both take a query filter and an update document. (low confidence)
bulk_write accepts a list of operation hashes covering insert_one, update_one, update_many, replace_one, delete_one and delete_many. (medium confidence)
Each Mongo::Client has a connection pool for each server in the topology. Connections are reused, and without a configured min_pool_size, pools open connections on demand. (low confidence)
max_pool_size limits concurrent pooled connections per server, while max_connecting limits concurrent connection establishment per pool; these are different capacity controls. (medium confidence)
The connection-options reference distinguishes server_selection_timeout, which bounds waiting for server selection, from connection-pool capacity settings. (low confidence)

The shared connection-pooling specification requires thread-safe pool behavior but explicitly declares connections and pools not fork-safe; its reset-after-fork procedure clears pools and closes connections in the child. This is a specification requirement, not verification of a particular Ruby release’s fork hooks. (low confidence)

Each Mongo::Client maintains a pool per topology server. Pool capacity and concurrent connection creation are separate controls: max_pool_size limits pool size and max_connecting limits parallel connection establishment. (medium confidence)

The Ruby connection-options reference expresses connect_timeout and server_selection_timeout in seconds, while the corresponding URI options are connectTimeoutMS and serverSelectionTimeoutMS in milliseconds. The reference describes timeout_ms as an operation timeout in milliseconds. (medium confidence)
